name: Iran APT35 — Charming Kitten / Phosphorus
author: Threat Intelligence Team
prerequisites: Email gateway logs available with full header information
Azure AD / Google Workspace sign-in logs accessible
Browser extension audit capability on managed endpoints
MFA logs capturing authentication method type (SMS, app, hardware key)
required_tools: Microsoft 365 Defender Threat Explorer or equivalent
Azure AD Sign-in log analysis (Splunk or Sentinel)
Browser management console (Chrome Enterprise, Intune) for extension auditing

hunt_actions.title: Credential Phishing and Account Takeover Detection
actions: Hunt for successful logins immediately after a password reset (APT35 resets passwords after credential phishing to lock out legitimate owner): `index=azure_ad OperationName='Change user password' | join UserPrincipalName [search index=azure_ad OperationName='User logged in' | where _time > relative_time(now(), '-1h')] | table _time, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, Location, ResultDescription`

Detect impossible travel following credential theft: Sentinel KQL: `SigninLogs | where ResultType == 0 | summarize Locations=make_set(Location), IPs=make_set(IPAddress) by UserPrincipalName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h) | where array_length(Locations) > 2 | project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, Locations, IPs`

hunt_actions.title: Malicious Browser Extension and Cookie Theft
actions: Audit Chrome extensions for unauthorized installs (APT35 uses malicious extensions for cookie/session theft — HYPERSCRAPE): `Get-ItemProperty 'HKCU:\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\*' | Select PSChildName, @{n='Path';e={$_.path}} | Export-Csv chrome_extensions.csv` — compare extension IDs against Chrome Web Store approved list; any extension loaded from a local path or unknown ID requires analysis

Hunt for browser session cookie theft indicators (new device login with session token after no credential prompt): Sentinel KQL: `SigninLogs | where AuthenticationRequirement == 'singleFactorAuthentication' and isnotempty(DeviceDetail.deviceId) | where DeviceDetail.deviceId !in (<approved_device_ids>) | project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, DeviceDetail.displayName, IPAddress, Location`

hunt_actions.title: HYPERSCRAPE Email Exfiltration Tool Detection
actions: Hunt for HYPERSCRAPE indicators — it downloads Gmail/Yahoo/Outlook email via IMAP with specific user-agent patterns: `index=proxy OR index=network cs-user-agent IN (*Python*,*python-requests*,*libcurl*) cs-uri-stem IN (*mail.google.com*,*imap.gmail.com*,*imap.mail.yahoo.com*,*outlook.office365.com*) | stats count by src_ip, cs-user-agent, cs-uri-stem | sort -count` — programmatic IMAP/API mail access from unexpected IPs is a HYPERSCRAPE indicator

Detect unusual OAuth token grants for mail access: `AuditLogs | where OperationName == 'Consent to application' and TargetResources[0].type == 'ServicePrincipal' | where AdditionalDetails contains 'Mail.Read' or AdditionalDetails contains 'Mail.ReadAll' | project TimeGenerated, InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName, TargetResources[0].displayName, AdditionalDetails`

hunt_actions.title: Infrastructure Reconnaissance and Pretexting
actions: Hunt for APT35-linked infrastructure using passive DNS — known APT35 C2 domain patterns include free TLD abuse and typosquat on academic/news/government domains: Cross-reference outbound DNS queries against VirusTotal PDNS: `curl -s 'https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/<domain>/resolutions?limit=10' -H 'x-apikey: <key>' | jq '.data[].attributes | {ip_address, date: .date}'` — also check URLScan.io: `curl -s 'https://urlscan.io/api/v1/search/?q=domain:<domain>&size=10' -H 'API-Key: <key>'`

Detect LinkedIn and social media credential harvesting infrastructure (APT35 creates fake LinkedIn researcher profiles): Monitor for outbound connections to typosquat LinkedIn domains: `index=proxy cs-uri-stem=*linkedln* OR cs-uri-stem=*1inkedin* OR cs-uri-stem=*linked-in* | stats count by src_ip, cs-uri-stem | sort -count` — also alert on: connections to linke-din[.]com, linkedln[.]com or similar registered within last 30 days

questions: Are all user accounts, especially those of executives, researchers, journalists, and policy staff, enrolled in phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn hardware keys or Microsoft Authenticator with number matching), rather than SMS-based MFA which APT35 is known to bypass via SIM swapping?
Is there a process for employees to report suspicious contact from unknown individuals on LinkedIn, WhatsApp, or Signal claiming to be researchers or journalists — a known APT35 pretexting vector?
Are browser extensions audited and allowlisted via endpoint management (Chrome Enterprise, Intune), with unauthorized extensions blocked from installation on managed devices?

Are OAuth application consent grants reviewed and restricted — is the user consent workflow blocked for apps requesting Mail.Read, Files.ReadAll, or other sensitive permissions, requiring admin approval instead?
Are Azure AD Conditional Access policies configured to block sign-ins from Tor exit nodes, VPN services, and hosting provider IP ranges commonly used by APT35 for anonymization?
Are IMAP and POP3 access to mailboxes blocked for standard users, with only approved clients using modern authentication permitted to access email programmatically?
Is there a threat intelligence subscription or ISAC membership providing timely notification of APT35/Charming Kitten infrastructure and IOC updates relevant to the organization's sector?

Are personnel in roles targeted by APT35 (academics, nuclear researchers, defense policy analysts, government officials) provided with additional security awareness training specific to nation-state social engineering techniques?
